findings.statement: with uniform keys the range flush changes nothing: device bytes within 1.05x and ingest a tie
findings.detail: device bytes 9.2 MB with the range flush against 9.2 with the full one (1.000x); ingest 514468 against 518813 ops/s (ranges vs full: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.992, p=0.8345) -- within noise, not a result); partitions 1 against 1. Every range holds pieces after a uniform load, so selecting the ranges with pieces selects them all

findings.statement: with sequential keys the range flush cuts device bytes to at most 0.6x the full flush's
findings.detail: device bytes 9.2 MB with the range flush against 9.2 with the full one (1.000x) at 16 MB seals; disk 3.3 against 3.3 MB, partitions 1 against 1. A seal of ordered keys lands in one or two ranges, and only those are rewritten

findings.statement: with sequential keys the range flush lifts ingest-to-routed by at least 1.2x
findings.detail: 517414 ops/s with the range flush against 522447 with the full one (ranges vs full: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.990, p=0.4034) -- within noise, not a result); merge phase 0.011s against 0.010s, seal 0.012s against 0.012s. The drain's merge shrinks with the bytes it rewrites

findings.statement: reads after the drain do not differ between the two flushes under either key order
findings.detail: uniform: 121 ns per read with the range flush against 113 (ranges vs full: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.068, p=0.0927) -- within noise, not a result); sequential: 118 against 118 (ranges vs full: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.998, p=0.9362) -- within noise, not a result). Both flushes leave a fully routed store, and the range flush keeps the boundaries where they were

notes: four arms interleaved in one process, fresh store per rep, at 16 MB seals over 64 MB partitions -- the shape f52 priced at 1.5x the device bytes -- with the drain inside the window. Two key orders: uniform (a random permutation of the ids) and sequential (the ids in order, the shape of a log). Two flushes: full (re-partition everything from every key, the original) and ranges (merge only the ranges that hold pieces, under the live fences). Device and disk bytes, phases, partitions, and point reads after the drain
